title: Finish the harness
prompt:
harness(bufs) returns the lines that go inside main, as a list of strings. bufs is a list of (slot, data) pairs for i32 buffers, already in slot order. The array lines are written. Two things are missing:

  • The call passes nothing. Make it pass every array in order, like kernel(b0, b1);.
  • After the call, add one print line per element, buffer by buffer. print_line(slot, i) builds the line for you.

The tests show the lines joined with | .

tests.expect:
static int32_t b0[3] = {10, 20, 0}; | kernel(b0); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[2]);

static int32_t b0[1] = {7}; | static int32_t b1[2] = {0, 0}; | kernel(b0, b1); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[0]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[1]);

static int32_t b0[2] = {-1, 2}; | static int32_t b1[1] = {3}; | static int32_t b2[2] = {4, 5}; | kernel(b0, b1, b2); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("1 %d
", (int)b1[0]); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[0]); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[1]);

static int32_t b0[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0}; | kernel(b0); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[0]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[1]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[2]); | printf("0 %d
", (int)b0[3]);

static int32_t b2[1] = {9}; | static int32_t b5[2] = {8, -7}; | kernel(b2, b5); | printf("2 %d
", (int)b2[0]); | printf("5 %d
", (int)b5[0]); | printf("5 %d
", (int)b5[1]);

hints: The call needs one name per buffer: `b0`, `b1` and so on. Build each name from `slot`, then join them with `", "` the same way `init` is built.
The prints come after the call, so they need a second loop over `bufs`. Inside it, loop `i` over `range(len(data))`.
The call is `"kernel(" + ", ".join(f"b{slot}" for slot, _ in bufs) + ");"`. Each print is `lines.append(print_line(slot, i))`.
explain: A harness is three groups of lines: one array per buffer filled with its starting data, one call to `kernel` with the arrays in slot order, and one print per element. The prints must come after the call, because the kernel changes the arrays in place.
